who.value: buyer who raised a return, and the seller receiving it

job.value: buyer tracks the request; seller reviews it and accepts or declines

arrivedFrom.value: order details or a notification about the request

questions.title: The screen's job is clear from the first screen
questions.why: 'Return/refund details' with 'Reviewing your request' (buyer) and 'Buyer submitted a return/refund request' (seller) state the screen's purpose.

questions.title: The action that does the job stands out most
questions.why: The seller's 'Review request' and buyer's 'Cancel request' are solid teal but only appear as a sticky bar after scrolling; at first view the status cards dominate.

questions.title: Every label says what happens when tapped
questions.why: 'Review request', 'Cancel request', 'View details', 'View order details' and 'Copy' all predict what happens.

questions.title: No terms this user wouldn't know
questions.why: Terms like 'Return item, full refund' and 'Buyer Protection' are familiar to someone in a post-purchase dispute.

questions.title: Only asks what this user can decide at this stage
questions.why: The buyer only waits or cancels and the seller reviews, both things they can decide now.

questions.title: Advanced detail is tucked away
questions.why: Per-item 'View details' tucks specifics away, but the long 'Order ID DASD-FSWDHEG…' and 'Order time' sit inline on the main view.

questions.title: Everything fits this stage and this user
questions.why: Status, items, refund amount and support links all belong to an open return.

questions.title: Little reading needed to act
questions.why: The seller's status card is a three-line sentence with a deadline, though the amount 'S$955.00' and item rows read at a glance.
